item.title: Report: Dolphins DT Zach Sieler to have season-ending biceps surgery
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Dolphins will reportedly be without one of their top defensive players for the rest of the season.
item.content:encoded:
The Dolphins will reportedly be without one of their top defensive players for the rest of the season.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that defensive tackle Zach Sieler tore his biceps early in Sunday's loss to the Lions. He was able to play the rest of the game, but needs to have surgery that will end his season.

Sieler started the first eight games of the season for the Dolphins. He had 24 tackles and two sacks in those appearances. He joined the team during the 2019 season and has 377 tackles, 37.5 sacks, two interceptions, five forced fumbles and six fumble recoveries during his time in Miami.

Sieler signed a three-year extension with the Dolphins ahead of the 2025 season. The deal ties him to the team through the 2029 season with cap hits of more than $20 million each year.

item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Bengals are bringing in some help for their defensive front.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals are bringing in some help for their defensive front.

Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Cincinnati is trading for Philadelphia edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie.

The Eagles will receive a 2027 sixth-round pick to complete the deal.

Ebiketie signed a one-year deal with Philadelphia in March. He’s recorded 25 total tackles this season with two QB hits in nine games.

A second-round pick in 2022, Ebiketie has recorded 16.5 sacks in his 76 career games.

item.title: Cardinals add QB Joey Aguilar off Jaguars' practice squad
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: After trading quarterback Jacoby Brissett, and then losing his replacement Gardner Minshew to a potentially season-ending elbow injury, the Cardinals are bringing in quarterback reinforcements.
item.content:encoded:
After trading quarterback Jacoby Brissett, and then losing his replacement Gardner Minshew to a potentially season-ending elbow injury, the Cardinals are bringing in quarterback reinforcements.

Joey Aguilar will join the Cardinals' 53-player roster from the Jaguars' practice squad, according to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.

The 25-year-old Aguilar was the starting quarterback for the Tennessee Volunteers last season and spent a total of seven years in college football, with two at City College of San Francisco, two at Diablo Valley College and two at Appalachian State before transferring to Tennessee.

The only healthy quarterback in Arizona right now is rookie Carson Beck. Aguilar will presumably back him up on Sunday against the Rams, and the Cardinals will likely add another quarterback to their practice squad or active roster this week.

item.title: The Vikings, as expected, are making calls about adding a quarterback
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The clock is ticking, and it won't be cheap to trade for a starter.
item.content:encoded:
They did it in 2016, after Teddy Bridgewater suffered a season-ending knee injury in late August. They did it in 2023, after Kirk Cousins suffered a season-ending torn Achilles tendon.

They're doing it today, in order to avoid having the season end at 6-11.

According to ESPNFL, the Vikings have begun making calls regarding a possible trade for a quarterback.

Of course they're making calls. Coach Kevin O'Connell made that fairly clear last night. The real question is whether they can get a deal done.

They're not operating from a position of strength, especially after a horrendous showing from Carson Wentz, whose passer rating against Buffalo was 8.9. The greater a team's perceived need, the more the other team will want.

The Vikings' best hope is to stumble into a situation where multiple teams are looking to unload a starter. By persuading one team that the Vikings will strike a deal with another team, the price could come down.

There aren't many current starters who would even possibly be available. Two of them — Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins and Colts quarterback Daniel Jones — have experience in Minnesota. Others include, potentially, Jets quarterback Geno Smith and Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert.

Backups could be available. Mac Jones had been linked to Minnesota in the past. The 49ers would have to feel comfortable with the alternative to Mac Jones as the understudy to Brock Purdy. If a team trades its No. 2, it assumes the risk that the starter will get injured in the very next game.

That happened to the Steelers in 2019. They traded Josh Dobbs to the Jaguars after Nick Foles was injured in Week 1. In Week 2, the Steelers lost Ben Roethlisberger for the year. Then came the Duck Hodges show.

At this point, it's fair to wonder whether a quarterback upgrade will even matter for the Vikings. The flaws in the offense may run deeper than the quarterback position.

Still, it's obvious that they need someone who can perform more efficiently than Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz, who in all fairness should be cut today.

And if the Vikings can't upgrade at quarterback, they need to listen to offers for receiver Justin Jefferson. His prime is being wasted, and he surely would love to move on (even if he'd never say that out loud).

The last-ditch effort could be to sign Jimmy Garoppolo, who would likely be an instant upgrade to the very low bar that Minnesota's current quarterbacks have established.

item.title: The Vikings need to trade for a quarterback tomorrow
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Failure to act leads to one conclusion: The Vikings are dysfunctional.
item.content:encoded:
The biggest test of the still-new partnership between Vikings G.M. Nolan Teasley and Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell has arrived.

What will they do about a team with a Super Bowl-caliber defense and an offense that could barely function in the MAC?

The window remains open until 4:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday. The Vikings were in this spot three years ago, when Kirk Cousins tore an Achilles tendon two days before the deadline.

That time, the Vikings didn't have many options; they ended up with Josh Dobbs. This time, there are two former Vikings on other teams who know the Minnesota offense: Colts quarterback Daniel Jones and Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins.

If the calls haven't already been made, they should be. Immediately. What will it take to salvage a season that is disintegrating before everyone's eyes, despite the 6-2 record?

It wouldn't be easy to plug and play a new quarterback, but there's history with Jones and Cousins. It would be easier to get them up to speed than if they brought in someone who would be learning everything from scratch.

If, in the end, the Colts want too much for Jones and the Raiders want too much for Cousins (neither is untouchable; the question is the amount of the compensation), the only other starter potentially available would be Geno Smith.

Some have suggested a play for Justin Herbert. At this point, however, it's impossible to know whether his implosion is about his surroundings or about Herbert.

Then there's Jimmy Garoppolo, who remains a free agent — and who has been largely forgotten.

Whatever the Vikings do, staying the course with Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz is a middle finger to the fan base. And Max Brosmer, by all appearances, isn't good enough to make a difference.

The fans know it. The boos were frequent, loud, and warranted on Monday night.

So what will Teasley and O'Connell do?

And, perhaps more importantly, when will the narrative change about O'Connell being a quarterback whisperer? He didn't want 2024 first-rounder J.J. McCarthy, who had fallen to third on the depth chart before he was given away for a fifth-round draft pick. O'Connell preferred Murray, who has been underwhelming. Wentz landed at No. 2 on the depth chart, and when the lights got bright Wentz winced..

It's a pivotal moment for Teasley, O'Connell, and the entire franchise. They can continue to act like everything is fine, that 6-2 is a good record, whatever.

Anyone who's paying attention knows the truth. The Vikings, after starting 6-0, are sinking like a smooth stone in a septic tank. Failure to act amounts to dysfunction.

And, yes, dysfunctional teams do dysfunctional things. Some around the league have suggested in recent years that the Vikings are low-key dysfunctional.

Right or wrong, they're definitely the worst 6-2 team we've ever seen — and the only question at this point is whether they'll figure out how to win another game.

item.title: NFL reinstates WR Brandon Aiyuk from reserve/left squad list
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: 49ers' get a two-week roster exemption.
item.content:encoded:
Brandon Aiyuk is back, and the ball is in the 49ers' court.

The NFL reinstated the 49ers receiver from the reserve/left squad list on Monday. The league also gave the 49ers a two-week roster exemption, giving the team a window for making a decision about what to do with Aiyuk.

The 49ers now have an immediate decision to make about Aiyuk. If he's on the roster on Tuesday at 4:00 p.m. ET, he's owed a game check for the week.

Based on the Player Personnel Manual, placement on the reserve/left squad list apparently tolled his 2025 salary. That means he'll return to the $1.17 million base salary from 2025, with the 2026 salary of $26.015 million delayed until 2027.

It gives the 49ers a window to trade Aiyuk, with the new team getting him for the rest of the season at only $585,000 in non-guaranteed pay.

The 49ers can carry Aiyuk as an extra man on the roster until Monday, November 23.

It's unclear, currently, whether Aiyuk agreed to refund past bonus money to the 49ers in order to get the league to reinstate him. If the 49ers trade or release Aiyuk, the 49ers lose the ability to get money back from Aiyuk.

item.title: Jesse Minter does not address Lamar Jackson's injury, says he'll keep conversations with QB private
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Over the weekend, reporting emerged that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he intends to return to play in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Over the weekend, reporting emerged that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he intends to return to play in 2026.

Baltimore head coach Jesse Minter, however, was not inclined to give any update on the star QB in his Monday press conference.

Jackson is reportedly out for 6-9 weeks with a fractured and dislocated thumb. He is currently on injured reserve.

Minter was asked what the chance is that Jackson will be able to return this season.

“You know, I’m going to keep most of the conversations between Lamar and I between Lamar and I,” Minter said. “Again, just like before, it’s a guy when you’re dealing with something, that no one wants to be on the field more. He’s probably going to do everything he can to put himself in position [to play]. But I’ll leave it at that.”

Minter also did not say whether or not Jackson requires or already has had surgery.

“I’m going to keep all that stuff between me and him,” Minter said.

Does that mean the public won’t know the nature of Jackson’s injury and if he can return?

“You may know, but that’ll come from him,” Minter said.

There was one more follow-up in the press conference, with Minter being asked if it’s accurate to say Jackson’s thumb was fractured and dislocated.

Minter chuckled before saying, “Again, that is specifics. I’ll keep it between me and him.”

Jackson has technically started five games this season. But he played just a half against Tennessee and threw only one pass against Buffalo before having to exit due to injury.

Jacoby Brissett is now set to take over as Baltimore’s starting quarterback with Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve.

item.title: Report: Jaguars plan to keep Brian Thomas Jr. at trade deadline
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Jaguars have been bringing players in to fortify the roster for a deep postseason run.
item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars have been bringing players in to fortify the roster for a deep postseason run.

They don’t intend to send one out.

Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports the Jaguars plan to keep receiver Brian Thomas Jr. — barring a surprise.

Thomas has been rumored to be on the trade block largely due to his lack of production this season. He’s received just 22 targets in eight games, catching 10 passes for 117 yards with two touchdowns.

The No. 23 overall pick of the 2024 draft, Thomas caught 87 passes for 1,282 yards with 10 touchdowns as a rookie. But his production dipped even last year — the first season under head coach Liam Coen — with Thomas catching just 48 passes for 707 yards with two TDs.

Even with Fowler’s report, plans can change. If a team seriously needs a receiver and is willing to pony up, the Jaguars may change their mind about dealing Thomas before the 4 p.m. ET deadline.

item.title: Jordan Davis is "a little disappointed" to be traded by Eagles
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: For players with no-trade clauses and most starting-level quarterbacks, there's no reason to worry about a rogue wind blowing them to a new team in a new city.
item.content:encoded:
For players with no-trade clauses and most starting-level quarterbacks, there's no reason to worry about a rogue wind blowing them to a new team in a new city. For everyone else, it can happen at any time.

It happened on Monday to defensive tackle Jordan Davis. After the deal was done that sent him to the Jaguars for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick, Davis commented on the situation.

"A little disappointed but, you know, understanding that they're in the rebuilding process glad and you know, for the picks — first-round and second-round pick — obviously helps the team and, you know, I love those guys," Davis told Jeff Sversky of Fox 29. "So however I can help the team, even in my departure, I’m absolutely glad to be doing that."

He may or may not be glad for the likely uptick in his workload. In Philly, Davis was on the field for 52 percent of the snaps. Given what the Jaguars gave up for him, they'll need more than that to justify the trade.

Either way, it's part of life in the NFL. Even though the 32 businesses are independent, they're branches of the same tree. An involuntary transfer is always a possibility for the vast majority of players.

item.title: Jaguars trades for Jessie Bates, Jordan Davis could complicate deadline deals
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: It's Let's Make A Deal day in the NFL, with the window on trades closing at 4:00 p.m.
item.content:encoded:
It's Let's Make A Deal day in the NFL, with the window on trades closing at 4:00 p.m. ET. And the deals made on Monday could become a complication.

The Jaguars gave up a lot for two of the three players they acquired. As to safety Jessie Bates III, it was a second-round pick and a fifth-round pick. For defensive tackle Jordan Davis (a run-stopper with 52-percent playing time), it was a first-round pick and a second-round pick.

Those deals will hover over today's talks. Teams that are considering trading players will, at some level, be concerned about the perception that they didn't get enough, relative to what the Jaguars invested on Monday.

If the Jaguars intended that, they're next-level super geniuses. Go all in, acquire players who'll help the team get to the Super Bowl and win it, and make it harder for other contenders to do the same thing today.

As it relates to Jacksonville receiver Brian Thomas Jr., a first-round pick in 2024 who had 1,282 yards as a rookie and doesn't fit the current offense, that could also result in a better haul, if/when the Rams join the effort (which includes the Chiefs, Steelers, and Commanders) to wrest Thomas away from the Jaguars.

Regardless of the motivation(s), Monday's trades by the Jaguars could make it harder for deals to get done on Tuesday. Most notably, it could make the Colts decide not to take the best offer on the table for running back Jonathan Taylor.

With the Giants offering a two and a five, would the Colts be willing to accept for Taylor what the Jaguars gave up for Bates? How much more will it take to get the Colts to believe it's a proper return given the investment made in getting Bates?

However it plays out, if not much happens at the deadline, the wrench thrown into the gears by the Jaguars could be a factor in that.

item.title: Justin Jefferson: Vikings' offense didn't get it done, we've got to figure it out
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Jefferson finished with three catches for 58 yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson has been visibly frustrated on the field the last two weeks as the offense hasn't been able to move the ball in back-to-back losses. After Monday night's loss to the Bills, he said the offense needs to stop squandering the work of a great defense.

"The offense didn't get it done," Jefferson said. "Defense did a phenomenal job once again, getting it done against a very good offense. We've got to figure it out on offense."

Jefferson said everyone on the offense has to do better, although he admitted he doesn't know all the answers.

"We've got to figure it out," Jefferson said. "That's something we don't have the answer to at the moment. We've just got to figure it out."

Although quarterback Carson Wentz was terrible on Monday night, and Kyler Murray hasn't been much better for most of the season, Jefferson called it "an all 11 thing" and said it's not just on the quarterback.

"It doesn't really matter who's throwing the ball, as long as it gets to us, that's all that matters, and it's up to us to make those plays. It's tough. Definitely tough," Jefferson said.

The Vikings' offense has been tough to watch.

item.title: Vikings' 17:28 time of possession was their lowest in franchise history
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Minnesota Vikings have played 1,064 games in the history of their franchise, which started in 1961.
item.content:encoded:
The Minnesota Vikings have played 1,064 games in the history of their franchise, which started in 1961. Before yesterday, they had never played a game in which they possessed the ball for less than 17 and a half minutes. Now they have.

The Vikings' time of possession of 17:28 in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Bills was their lowest in franchise history.

The previous franchise low was 17:38, set in the NFC Championship Game after the 2000 season, when the Vikings lost to the Giants 41-0.

On Monday night, the Vikings' offense could not stay on the field. The first quarter set the tone: They had three possessions, which were two three-and-outs and one possession on which they lost a fumble on the first play. Their longest possession of the night lasted 3:11, and on that possession they ran five plays, totaled just 10 yards, and punted.

The Vikings' defense played well, but not so well that the Bills weren't able to sustain some long drives, including three drives that took more than six minutes off the clock. The Bills gained 22 first downs; the Vikings gained just nine.

The Bills' 42:32 time of possession was their second-best in franchise history, trailing only a 1989 game in which they possessed the ball for 42:53 and beat the Jets 34-3.

item.title: Sean McVay on Puka Nacua injury: I'd be lying if I said I wasn't questioning that play call
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is set to go on injured reserve after suffering MCL, PCL and turf toe injuries in Sunday's win over the Commanders.
item.content:encoded:
Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is set to go on injured reserve after suffering MCL, PCL and turf toe injuries in Sunday's win over the Commanders.

Nacua's injuries occurred on the Rams' final offensive play when he was tackled after rushing for five yards on third-and-11. Nacua took a handoff on the play and head coach Sean McVay was asked at a Monday press conference if he second-guessed himself for putting Nacua in position to take a hit at that point in the game.

McVay said he's "kicking myself about those kinds of things" and called it something the Rams have to think about "internally" as they move forward.

"I’d be lying to you if I said I haven't questioned the decision-making on that last play over and over in my head of what could have been another option that you felt like could have gotten a conversion, and maybe ended the game that would've led to him not taking a violent hit to his right knee," McVay said. "It's stuff that I feel tremendous responsibility for, and we've got to be able to figure out how to protect these guys while also putting them in positions that help our team and allow them to be able to shine. He's a guy we have to be intentional about because it's a bummer. Because he can do so much, you want to make sure you don't take that for granted."

With Nacua and Davante Adams now out for the indefinite future, the Rams may be in the market for receiving help before the trade deadline passes at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday. They do not have their 2027 first- or third-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick or their 2029 third-round pick thanks to their trades for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie.

item.title: Carson Wentz: This one felt pretty terrible
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Vikings' quarterback had perhaps the worst game any NFL quarterback has had this season in Monday night's loss to the Bills.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz had perhaps the worst game any NFL quarterback has had this season in Monday night's loss to the Bills. He didn't sugarcoat it afterward.

“This one felt pretty terrible. I’m not going to lie," Wentz said, via the Associated Press.

Wentz completed 8 of 25 passes for 81 yards, with no touchdowns and two interceptions against the Bills. His passer rating of 8.9 was the lowest for any quarterback in any game in which he threw more than three passes this season. Wentz said he knows the Vikings' defense can win with competent quarterback play, and he did not provide that.

“To go kind of lay an egg, personally, the way I struggled early, especially with our defense playing as good as they’ve been all year, honestly," Wentz said. "They did it again tonight, and we just didn’t help them out. I didn’t help them out. It’s hard to put my finger on the why.”

The Vikings need to put their finger on the how, as in how to fix their offense. Or else a great defense is going to waste.

item.title: James Cook's 31 carries vs. Vikings were the most in any NFL game this season
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Against a Vikings defense that has been teeing off on opposing quarterbacks this season, Bills coach Joe Brady knew he needed to lean on his running back on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
Against a Vikings defense that has been teeing off on opposing quarterbacks this season, Bills coach Joe Brady knew he needed to lean on his running back on Monday night.

And so he did, with Bills running back James Cook getting 31 carries for 107 yards and a touchdown in a 23-6 win over the Vikings.

Cook's 31 carries were the most any running back has had in any NFL game this season.

Cook led the NFL with 1,621 rushing yards last season, but he's actually been even more productive so far this season. He's averaging both more carries per game and more yards per game in 2026 than he did in 2025. Josh Allen makes the Bills' offense go, but the Bills rely on their running back as much as any team in the NFL, and on Monday night, Cook delivered.

item.title: Todd Monken not ready to name starter at QB for Week 10
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Shedeur Sanders has given Todd Monken something to think about.
item.content:encoded:
Shedeur Sanders has given Todd Monken something to think about.

The Browns' head coach told reporters in his Monday news conference that he's not ready to name a starter at quarterback for the Week 10 matchup against the Texans.

That came after Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reported that Deshaun Watson would be back in the saddle after missing Sunday's game.

"I really haven’t thought through it other than getting through this morning’s tape," Monken said. "I just got done meeting with the guys. They’ll flush the game and then we’ll have a chance to meet offensively more [extensively] later today. We went through the tape, immediately had to break, go to personnel, then the team comes in, and we haven’t had a chance to circle back as an offensive staff."

Watson started the first eight games of the season for Cleveland, generating five game-winning drives for the team’s five wins.

Sanders, who started after Watson missed the first two days of the practice week while in concussion protocol, completed 19-of-31 passes for 297 yards with two touchdowns and no picks against the Saints.

“Well I’m awfully proud of him,” Monken said of Sanders. “It’s been 10 weeks since he had reps with the ones. I think it showed up, the reps that we gave him in camp.

“I thought he battled. I thought he showed composure in the pocket, getting to his check-downs at times. He made plays with his feet in escaping. He made the scramble play to Jerry [Jeudy]. He made a big third-down conversion early and he made one right there in four-minute, right before the holding call that gave us a first down. So, that’s what you wanted to see.”

Monken noted that philosophically, he doesn’t really think of a player losing a job due to injury.

“It’s week to week,” Monken said. "A player doesn’t lose or win a job — I don’t know what that means. Each week, we put the best players on the field that give us a chance to win.”

Monken added that Sanders’ play didn’t necessarily alter his thinking about whether or not Sanders could play at some point this season.

“I was thrilled. I was happy for him,” Monken said. “Every player wants to go and play and play well. And there were moments [where] I didn’t coach well enough, he didn’t play well enough. But there were moments at the end of the game where he made plays, right? He got it in the players’ hands, did a really good job, was in command. So, I was really pleased for him. And I was hopeful he’d play well. I thought he had a great week of practice and there is no guarantee that will carry over. So I’m really happy for him.

“Does it give me confidence? From what I saw in the fall, you bet it does. It gives me more and more confidence that what I saw in the fall, there’s something to build on — for sure.”

We’ll see how that translates as the season continues. But the fact that Sanders played well enough to make it an open question does say something about his development.

item.title: Andy Reid: Patrick Mahomes day-to-day with elbow injury
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Reid said he had seen Mahomes on Monday and the QB was in "good spirits."
item.content:encoded:
While Patrick Mahomes' elbow injury looked bad when it happened on Sunday, he was able to finish the game, helping power the Chiefs to a 35-12 win over the Jets.

It sounds like he might not miss any further playing time either.

"Patrick, he is really day-to-day right now," head coach Andy Reid told reporters in his Monday news conference. "It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick. It looks like it’s just a matter of some rehab in there and getting rid of some of the soreness. And we’ll just see where it goes from there.

"But he’s in good spirits today — I have seen him today, so he’s in good spirits today."

Mahomes suffered the injury late in the first half. In the third quarter, he completed 7-of-10 passes for 81 yards. He was 5-of-6 for 41 yards in the fourth quarter.

Additionally, Reid mentioned Xavier Worthy (hamstring) and Jaylon Moore (ankle) are day-to-day with their respective injuries.

The Chiefs will be on the road to play the Falcons in Week 10. The first injury report of the week will be issued on Wednesday.

item.title: Gardner Minshew having tests on right arm after injury on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew remained in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks after hurting his right arm late in the first half, but his status for the team's Week 10 game against the Rams is not certain.
item.content:encoded:
Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew remained in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks after hurting his right arm late in the first half, but his status for the team's Week 10 game against the Rams is not certain.

Head coach Mike LaFleur said at a Monday press conference that Minshew is undergoing tests on his arm and he said it is a possibility that he will not be able to play this week.

The Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens last week, which puts third-round pick Carson Beck in position to start if Minshew is unable to play. Beck has not appeared in any games yet this season.

Minshew's injury is one of several negative injury updates LaFleur delivered on Monday. He also announced that wide receiver Michael Wilson is out for the year with a neck injury and that center Hjalte Froholdt is in the concussion protocol.

item.title: Eagles say Jaguars made an offer they couldn't refuse for Jordan Davis
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Eagles announced the trade that sent defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jaguars, saying the "Jaguars made an offer that executive vice president/General Manager Howie Roseman simply could not refuse."
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles announced the trade that sent defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jaguars, saying the "Jaguars made an offer that executive vice president/General Manager Howie Roseman simply could not refuse."

The Jaguars are sending a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles.

"We are extremely grateful to Jordan for his contributions to our team on the field and in the Philadelphia community since we drafted him five years ago," the team said in a statement. "He has been a key contributor to our team culture and on-field success, which included two Super Bowl appearances and a world championship in 2024. His growth and development as both a player and a leader are a testament to his hard work and character. We wish Jordan nothing but continued success."

The Eagles now have first-round picks in the 2027 draft, two first-round picks and two second-round picks in the 2028 draft and multiple second-round picks in 2029.

The Eagles made Davis a first-round pick in 2022, and he totaled 193 tackles, 9.5 sacks, 15 quarterback hits and 11 passes defensed in 73 games.

item.title: Receiver-needy teams should call about Justin Jefferson
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: If the Vikings aren't going to upgrade at QB, they should give Jefferson a chance at a championship.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson is the ultimate team player. And he'd ultimately never say publicly if he wanted to be traded to a new team.

Teams looking for a receiver should make the call.

Few players are untouchable, when it comes to a trade. And even if the Vikings would hang up the phone and not listen, teams that need a high-end pass-catcher should try.

The Rams currently are in a pickle, thanks to the placement of Puka Nacua on injured reserve, where he joins Davante Adams. The Chiefs could use help at the position, too.

Ditto for the Steelers, who (like the Chiefs and Commanders) have interest in Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr.

Then there are the 49ers, who are always lurking when it comes to possibly making a big move.

Regardless, it makes sense to make the call. If the Vikings aren't going to make a move for a functional quarterback, they should stockpile picks and give Jefferson a chance to chase the championship that won't happen in Minnesota — especially if they waste his seventh season by not upgrading at the quarterback position.

Yes, a trade would come with a 2027 cap charge. The Vikings also would avoid the $30 million he's due to make in 2027, and the upgrade to meet the increased market that he surely already wants.

At the end of the day, it's one or the other. Trade for a better quarterback, or trade Jefferson to another team. Of the available options, doing neither makes the least sense.

item.title: Kevin O'Connell on potential quarterback trade: "I'll defer to Nolan [Teasley] on that"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Vikings coach doesn't rule out making a deal by Tuesday's deadline.
item.content:encoded:
After Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Bills, during which Carson Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards, two interceptions, and an 8.9 passer rating, Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was asked whether the team will consider trying to acquire a quarterback by the trade deadline at 4:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday.

"I'll defer to [G.M.] Nolan [Teasley] on that," O'Connell said. "We've had dialogue about a lot of different positions. And tight turnaround obviously playing the Monday night game before that, and we'll get right to work on any potential moves that can be there. But really just focused on the game tonight, which was not good enough in any way, shape, or form."

No, it wasn't. It was worse than horrible.

O'Connell was asked at one point whether he has ever felt as challenging as it does right now, as a play-caller.

"No," he said.

They have options. Several teams could be looking to make a deal. And even if it won't be cheap, it's necessary to salvage what was, only nine days ago, a very promising season.

It still can be. A return of Kirk Cousins would be a B-12 shot to the franchise. Even Daniel Jones would make things better than they are.

And if they want to go all in, try to make a deal for Justin Herbert — who may be thrilled at this point to don an eye patch and escape from L.A.

Whatever the Vikings do, they need to do something. Otherwise, there may not be a quarterback change when the season ends.

There could be a coaching change.

item.title: Nick Sirianni: We'll talk about possible staff changes during bye week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Eagles lost their seventh straight game on Sunday and they'll head into their bye week with little hope of salvaging anything over their final eight regular season games.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles lost their seventh straight game on Sunday and they'll head into their bye week with little hope of salvaging anything over their final eight regular season games.

That's shifted the focus in Philadelphia to what kinds of changes may be coming for the team. Head coach Nick Sirianni was asked if there's any chance of those changes starting with alterations to the coaching staff during the week off.

"We'll talk. Obviously, right now my job is to be there for our guys and to go watch the tape and go look through everything," Sirianni said, via a transcript from the team. "I think we always think — we'll do everything. I'll do anything I can to help this team win football games. Like I said, I'll look at myself internally first and then go from there. My job is to coach the players and to coach the coaches, and anything I can do to help this team win games, we'll do. Everything can always be on the table, but I don't think you change just to change because that's what your record says that -- you've got to look at what's really real and not react to anything else. Again, I just don't believe you just change just to change. If you have a strong reason to do things in anything, not just change, but in anything and you're convicted on it, that's how we'll go about our business."

Sirianni faced further questions about offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and changes on that side of the ball, but Sirianni said he was "not going to get into the hypotheticals" while reiterating that he's willing to do anything he can to make the team better. The coming days should bring more word about whether any of that will involve changes to his staff.

item.title: Klint Kubiak: We wouldn't be where we are without Kirk Cousins' "amazing" decision-making
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Raiders signed Kirk Cousins in April with the idea that he would start for the entire season while No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza develops.
item.content:encoded:
The Raiders signed Kirk Cousins in April with the idea that he would start for the entire season while No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza develops.

That plan has had solid returns, with Cousins completing 64.1 percent of his passes for 2,340 yards with 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions.

But three of those picks came in Sunday’s loss to the 49ers, which was Cousins’ worst game of the season. On Monday, head coach Klint Kubiak was asked about the QB’s decision-making on the giveaways.

“Kirk has been an extremely solid decision maker all season,” Kubiak said, via transcript from the team. “There’s ones he wants back. He wants back the first play of [the] second half. [He] wants back the one in the red zone where we did not give him protection to make a good decision. In the last play of the game, we’re trying to make a play, so he wants those back.

“But we’re not in the position that we are without the amazing decisions he’s made all year. So, we’ve got to coach up those ones and help him learn from them. But again, I’m very pleased with — the quarterback has to be the best decision-maker on the team, any organization. He wasn’t on those two plays, and that last one I’m calling a heave-ho.”

With the trade deadline rapidly approaching and the Raiders sitting at 4-5, there have been rumors about teams being interested in Cousins. Kubiak was asked how he thinks players like Cousins and Maxx Crosby — who expressed no interest in being traded — are handling that situation.

“Well, that’s the business that we’re in,” Kubiak said. “That’s the business of football, and those guys are veterans. They’ve been around that, so you just keep working. There’s a lot of things that are out of your control.”

If the Raiders were to trade Cousins, it would signal that the team feels Mendoza is ready to take over as starting quarterback. But because Las Vegas is still in the thick of things in the AFC as the current No. 9 seed, they may not be inclined to shake things up at the game’s most important position.

item.title: 2026 NFL Trade Deadline live updates: Tracker, deals, news, rumors, analysis
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Jordan Davis, Jeffery Simmons, DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson and more big-name NFL players are on the move.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, and PFT has you covered with news and analysis of every trade, potential trade, rumor of a trade and trade that won’t be happening.

Here’s what’s happening on the NFL trade front:

Jordan Davis to Jacksonville: The Eagles traded Davis to the Jaguars for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Will the Vikings trade for a quarterback? Coach Kevin O'Connell says he’ll defer to GM Nolan Teasley.

Giants are looking to add: John Harbaugh is prioritizing now over the future.

Will the Cowboys make any deadline deals? Team owner Jerry Jones doesn't see anything "significant" happening in Dallas.

Falcons agree to trade S Jessie Bates to the Jaguars: The Falcons will pick up most of Bates's remaining salary in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder.

Saints agree to trade DT Davon Godchaux to the Jaguars: The Jaguars doubled down on defensive additions.

Jets send Andre Cisco to Lions: The Lions are sending the Jets a 2028 sixth-round pick.

Bengals won't make a trade: Zac Taylor says they’re good where they are.

Jonathan Taylor trade appears likely: The Colts are expected to take the best offer they get for Taylor.

Jets LB Will McDonald requests a trade: The 2023 first-round pick would like to be on a new team.

Colts may trade more players: Indianapolis has told teams it wants more than a fourth-round pick for Josh Downs. Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones could both be traded, perhaps both to the Vikings.

Jacoby Brissett is headed to Baltimore: The Ravens and Cardinals announced a deal sending the veteran quarterback and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Ravens for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick.

Derrick Henry says he's not thinking about changing teams: The Ravens star expressed a desire to help the team improve after a fourth-straight loss.

Jonathan Taylor wants to know where he'll finish the season: Taylor said no one likes uncertainty when asked about talk that the Colts will trade him.

Chargers say they're not trading Khalil Mack: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said, "I want Khalil Mack to be here and Khalil Mack wants to be here."

Jeffery Simmons to Bears: Chicago receives Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Tennessee will receive 2027 and 2028 first-round picks along with a fourth-round pick in 2027.

Quenton Nelson to Seahawks: The Seahawks will send a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick back to Indianapolis.

DeForest Buckner to 49ers: Indianapolis will receive a 2027 fourth-round pick from San Francisco.

Jonathan Taylor trade talks have picked up: The Colts may not be done making deals.

The Jets have reportedly rebuffed Garrett Wilson trade interest: The Jets are not expected to deal their top wideout.

The Colts are open for business: Indianapolis is building for the future after firing General Manager Chris Ballard. Jonathan Taylor hasn’t requested a trade. Josh Downs says he's "open to whatever."

Budda Baker's name surfaces in trade rumors: Baker says he hasn’t asked to be traded from Arizona and also hasn't asked not to be traded.

Brian Thomas is a name to watch: The Jaguars trading Thomas frequently comes up in trade rumors.

Garrett Wilson wants to remain a Jet: The talented receiver says he is hoping not to get traded.

item.title: Jerry Jones doesn't expect a "significant trade" for Cowboys on Tuesday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has said repeatedly that he's open for business on the trade front, but every deal needs a partner and it doesn't sound like the Cowboys are finding much luck on that front.
item.content:encoded:
Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has said repeatedly that he's open for business on the trade front, but every deal needs a partner and it doesn't sound like the Cowboys are finding much luck on that front.

The trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday and Jones is heading toward that hour with low expectations for major changes to the roster.

“You know that old country song? When that phone’s not ringing, that’s me calling," Jones said on 105.3 The Fan. "It’s really not ringing, which you've heard me say numerous times — that's when you make a trade. Don’t count it out. A lot of things happen on that last day. But I don’t look for us to make a significant trade today.”

Jones did say that the team will make a move to address running back after losing Tyler Goodson to a knee injury, but he said he thinks that move is more likely to involve signing someone from outside the organization than it is to come via a trade.

item.title: Tom Brady sells stake in Birmingham City Football Club
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Tom Brady has a lot on his plate (but not any deli meat).
item.content:encoded:
Tom Brady has a lot on his plate (but not any deli meat). The man who is stretched even thinner than the most thinly-sliced slab of processed turkey has one less thing to compete for this time.

The Birmingham City Football Club has announced that Brady has exited the franchise.

"Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the Club over the last three years," the team said in a website post with the headline "Tom Brady Departure."

Brady acquired a minority share in the team, and became chairman of the advisory board, in August 2023, less than a year after his second and final retirement from the NFL.

Brady, whose other gigs include serving as Fox's top NFL analyst and owning a piece of the Raiders, made waves with comments made in a Birmingham City documentary (or, as most sports documentaries now are, an infomercial) regarding the work ethic of former club manager Wayne Rooney.

There's no reason to ever question Brady's work ethic. There are plenty of reasons to question whether he tries to do too much by wearing so many hats. There are only so many hours in the day, only so many days in the week.

He has written in his newsletter (assuming he even writes it) about balance. Maybe his decision to get out of the soccer business is about achieving better balance.

If, along the way, he got a nice return on his investment, even better for Brady. Especially since he seems to be in a race with Peyton Manning to acquire enough money to become the controlling owner of an NFL team.

The biggest problem is this. As Brady's net worth grows, the price tag for NFL ownership grows even faster.

Regardless, he likely now has more cash to add to the fund for potentially purchasing a franchise and, more importantly, one less thing to consume his time and attention.

item.title: Dan Campbell on benching Christian Mahogany: That's why I have team rules
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Lions guard Christian Mahogany had played every snap for five consecutive games until Sunday in Miami, when Mahogany didn't play at all and backup Miles Frazier took his place.
item.content:encoded:
Lions guard Christian Mahogany had played every snap for five consecutive games until Sunday in Miami, when Mahogany didn't play at all and backup Miles Frazier took his place. Lions coach Dan Campbell said his decision was for one reason only: Mahogany wasn't following team rules, and Frazier was.

Campbell didn't get into specifics about which rules Mahogany violated, but he said that even though the offensive line was struggling without Mahogany early in Sunday's win over the Dolphins, he never wavered in his belief that a player who hasn't been meeting expectations isn't going to play.

"Frazier earned that opportunity, and I thought he got better as the game went on, and you could say that about the whole unit — we were a little shaky early," Campbell said on 97.1 The Ticket.

Campbell said he won't talk publicly about what Mahogany did to earn the benching, but he did say Mahogany had broken a team rule more than once.

"That's really between us," Campbell said. "That's why I have team rules, that's why we have team rules and we've all got to abide by them, and if it's broken multiple times, then you do something about it. We're in good standing and like I said, the ball's in his court. It'll be good."

Campbell said Mahogany respects his decision, and that the whole team needs to understand that the head coach is going to hold every player to a high standard.

"Listen, we're good. He knows. We're all good. He'll be fine," Campbell said. "Look, if you say you're going to do something, you better hold up to it or otherwise you're going to lose the respect of people around you. Because if I'm sitting in that seat and I say one thing and then I don't do it, I'll immediately lose respect for that person. So we stick by what we say we're going to do here."

item.title: Liam Coen: "Definitely a curve" to getting Jessie Bates ready this week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jaguars made three trades on Monday, but their deal for safety Jessie Bates was the only one that was completed when head coach Liam Coen met with reporters on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars made three trades on Monday, but their deal for safety Jessie Bates was the only one that was completed when head coach Liam Coen met with reporters on Monday.

Coen called it a "no-brainer" to make a trade for a player who has shown the "ability to see things before they happen" on the field while also serving as a team captain in the locker room. Bates has been honing those skills for nine seasons, so he's gained quite a bit of experience but Coen said it will still be "definitely a curve" in terms of getting him acclimated to the Jaguars defense on the fly.

"You've seen it done so many ways, right? So many different examples of it being done," Coen said. "I know he's pretty intelligent, and he'll be able to understand a lot of that. It's more the checks and balances right in between plays, the communication from two by two to three by one, the motions, the checks. Like our verbiage where I would imagine three, cover three, cover four, you know, like the coverages, he'll understand and know and be able to play those, line up and play. It's more of the checks and balances and things that go into each play that we'll have to work through. We'll take it one day at a time, see what happens."

Defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux are the other new members of the Jaguars defense and the team's staff will be working overtime this week to make sure all of them are up to speed in time to face the Titans on Sunday.

item.title: PFT's Week 10 2026 NFL power rankings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Bills benefit from facing another backup QB.
item.content:encoded:
1. Bills (last week No. 1; 7-1): If they'd been playing a team with a borderline functional offense, they may have surrendered the top spot to Jacksonville.

2. Jaguars (No. 2; 6-2): Who cares about future draft picks when the AI apocalypse is coming?

3. 49ers (No. 3; 7-1): It feels like they'll be up to something on trade-deadline day.

4. Broncos (No. 4; 7-2): They're good enough to win the games they try to lose.

5. Bears (No. 5; 7-2): Caleb Williams isn't trying to become Patrick Mahomes; he's hoping to morph into Michael Jordan.

6. Chiefs (No. 7; 6-2): The kicker position shouldn't be a pick-your-poison proposition.

7. Steelers (No. 8; 6-2): Completing the sweep of the Bengals will be critical to winning the division.

8. Bengals (No. 11; 6-2): A Super Bowl push is very realistic.

9. Seahawks (No. 9; 5-4): Drew Lock fits this team better than Sam Darnold does.

10. Lions (No. 12; 6-2): What's German for kneecap?

11. Packers (No. 14; 6-3): When Micah Parsons returns, they could make a major move.

12. Vikings (No. 6; 6-2): Tuesday is arguably the most pivotal non-game day for the Vikings in years; will they upgrade at quarterback?

13. Giants (No. 16; 5-2-1): They're gradually pulling away in the NFC East.

14. Patriots (No. 10; 5-4): The regression continues.

15. Rams (No. 15; 5-4): Can Ty Simpson play receiver?

16. Browns (No. 13; 5-4): Can they stop the bleeding?

17. Raiders (No. 17; 4-5): It's time to flip the Fernando switch.

18. Buccaneers (No. 18; 3-6): They'd be dangerous on the road in the playoffs, if they can get there.

19. Ravens (No. 19; 4-5): Can they hold it together until Lamar Jackson returns?

20. Texans (No. 23; 3-5): C.J. Stroud is earning millions by the week.

21. Saints (No. 25; 3-5): Suddenly, they're tied for first place in the division.

22. Panthers (No. 22; 3-5): David Tepper is going to pull out all the stops in an effort to land Mike Tomlin.

23. Cardinals (No. 20; 3-6): Good news, Carson Beck — you're playing. Bad news, Carson Beck — you're playing.

24. Falcons (No. 21; 3-6): The Jessie Bates trade says it all; they're not interested in winning the division and getting blown out by the No. 5 seed in the wild-card round.

25. Cowboys (No. 26; 4-5): Even the games against the bad teams are a struggle.

26. Commanders (No. 24; 2-5-1): The mini-bye could be the time to bid farewell to the head coach.

27. Eagles (No. 27; 2-7): The soft-shell tank is on.

28. Titans (No. 28; 1-7): No one would have even noticed they were on a bye, but for whatever it was that happened with Calvin Ridley.

29. Colts (No. 29; 2-7): Vaya con dios, Jonathan Taylor.

30. Dolphins (No. 30; 1-7): The only drama left is whether they finish last in the division.

31. Jets (No. 31; 2-7): Same.

32. Chargers (No. 32; 0-8): Do they know they're winless?

item.title: Report: DT Jordan Elliott to work out for Bears
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Defensive tackle Jordan Elliott is getting another look from an NFL team.
item.content:encoded:
Defensive tackle Jordan Elliott is getting another look from an NFL team.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Elliott will work out for the Bears on Tuesday. It's the first time that Elliott has met with a team since being released by the Titans last month.

Elliott was released after he went to his car to retrieve a gun in the wake of an argument with Titans offensive tackle JC Latham. Defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers helped de-escalate the situation and Titans head coach Robert Saleh called Elliott a good person who had "a terrible lapse in judgment."

Saleh said he hoped Elliott would get another chance and it could come in Chicago. He had 11 tackles in five games with the Titans and started 64 games over six seasons with the 49ers and Browns to open his career.
